subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept this first-party external MXC sandbox plugin with the current native dependency graph and the MXC SDK's argv-carried base64 config transport after the stray sandbox export is removed?
rationale: The remaining non-code gates are security and supply-chain policy choices around a sandbox backend and native SDK dependency, which automation cannot approve safely.

options.title: Approve after export removal
options.body: Remove the accidental sandbox barrel export, then approve the exact head dependency graph and document acceptance of the preview MXC argv transport.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the plugin work open but block merge until MXC SDK offers a non-argv config transport or a maintainer-approved mitigation.

options.title: Move out of first-party repo
options.body: Ask the contributor to publish MXC independently through ClawHub until OpenClaw is ready to own the sandbox backend and dependency risk.

recommendation.title: Approve after export removal
recommendation.body: Remove the accidental sandbox barrel export, then approve the exact head dependency graph and document acceptance of the preview MXC argv transport.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current fix commit and have been driving the packaging and security-boundary review on this PR.
